buyer_added_terms.text: 1. Buyer Added Bid Specific Scope Of Work(SOW) Text Clause(s) SCOPE OF WORK Sl. N Activity Cod Scope of Work o. e Transportation of Fly ash/Bottom Ash from Silos/Surge Hoppe rs of TPS-II Expansion to Mine- II dumping yard with a lead of RMTHCIV 00 12 km in contractor's vehicle. The loading shall be done direc 1 70 tly from the Silos/ Surge hoppers. The vehicle transporting th e bottom ash shall be covered with Tarpaulin to avoid spillag e and dust. Transportation of Fly ash/Bottom Ash from Silos/Surge Hoppe rs of TPS-II Expansion to TPS-II Abandoned Ash Pond dumping RMTHCIV 00 yard (Stage-II) with a lead of 8.5 km in contractor's vehicle. T 2 71 he loading shall be done directly from the Silos/ Surge hoppe rs. The vehicle transporting the bottom ash shall be covered with Tarpaulin to avoid spillage and dust. Transportation of Fly ash/Bottom Ash from Silos/Surge Hoppe rs of TPS-II Expansion to the dumping yard of the abandoned RMTHCIV 00 pond of TPS-II (Stage-I) / interconnecting Ash Pond of TPS-II w 3 72 ith a lead of 5 km in contractor's vehicle. The vehicle transpo rting the bottom ash shall be covered with Tarpaulin to avoid spillage and dust. ***** 2. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses SPECIAL CONDITIONS Part-I 1.0 The contractor should be in possession of minimum two Tippers of minimum capacity of 7 tones in

his own name or should have Valid Lease agreement with the tipper's owner stating that the tipper c an be utilized for this work throughout the contract period. 2.0 The Bottom ash shall be transported and dumped at the Dumping yard of Mines-II/ Abandoned Ash Pond of TPS-II (Stage-II)/Abandoned Ash Pond of TPS-II (Stage-I) / Interconnection Pond of TPS-II as dir ected by the NLCIL officers with a lead of viz., 12 km, 8.5 km and 5 km from the silo/surge hoppers of TPS-II Expansion. If found dumped elsewhere, the same is to be transported to the Mine-II Dumping y ard / at the places shown by the departmental officers and a penalty equivalent to one third of unit r ate of the item will be deducted from the bill for the default quantity. 3.0 If required, the contractor should engage the tippers to transport the bed materials from any locatio n inside TPS II Expn to the designated dumping yards which are mentioned above. 4.0 No Lorries shall be engaged. 5.0 Over speed driving shall be avoided. 6.0 It is required to maintain the validity of the loading witness and gate pass in live condition at all tim es by the contractor. The supervisor shall report at the beginning of shift to know the requirement of tippers with respect to Bottom ash discharge in advance and to receive instructions from NLCIL Offic ers. 7.0 No female workers shall be engaged for the work. 8.0 The contractor shall supply necessary tools & PPEs to their Driver & Cleaner for loading and unloadi ng of Bottom ash and all safety measures while carrying out the work shall be ensured. 9.0 The contactor shall be prepared to engage sufficient number of tippers according to the quantum o f bottom ash accumulation and as demanded by the NLCIL officials and shall be able to complete the work within specified time for smooth running of units. The contractor shall carry out the work in rou nd the clock if required. 10.0 Transportation shall be done as per the requirement so that power generation is not affected due to non-removal of Bottom ash. 11.0 The contractor shall keep the tippers in good running condition at all times. 12.0 Before loading, the tipper shall be in empty condition. If it is found with load, penalty equivalent to o ne third of unit rate of the item for entire volume of tipper will be deducted from the bill. Tipper shoul d be loaded to its full capacity. 13.0 The tippers shall be operated only with the authorized drivers, failing; a penalty shall be imposed as directed by the Corporation Officials. The copy of the valid license of the drivers to be engaged for th e work shall be produced along with the original to the Departmental officers, while obtaining entry p ass to them. The original license will be returned after verification. 14.0 Non-removal of bottom ash due to non-engagement of sufficient tippers with loading cre w will be penalized at the rate of one third of unit rate of the item for each cum (M3) of B ottom ash accumulation. Apart from2penalty, the accumulated Bottom ash shall be cleared by en gaging other agency and the cost incurred for cleaning the accumulation will also be recovered from the bill of the contractor and necessary penal actions shall be taken as per the terms and conditions of the contract. 15.0 The contractor shall have to make necessary arrangements to unload the bottom ash at Mine- II Du mping Yard/Abandoned Ash Pond of TPS-II (Stage-II)/Abandoned Ash Pond of TPS-II (Stage-I) / Interco nnection Pond of TPS-I by creating the appropriate approaches to the unloading point on his own. 16.0 The contractor shall have close co-ordination in unloading points to monitor the Bottom ash / unloa ding works and monitor the leveling operations in the unloading area if required. The equipment req uired for leveling is in the scope of the contractor. 17.0 The loading of bottom ash shall be carried out in the presence of CISF personnel and the requisition for witnessing the loading shall be obtained in advance. 18.0 The out pass for the bottom ash load shall be entered with the signature of the witnessing CISF pers onnel, entry at the main gate of TPS-II Expn, entry at Old Main Gate (OMG) of Mine- II/Abandoned as h pond of TPS-II/E-Pond/Interconnecting Pond (If any arrangements are available) 19.0 The out passes shall be submitted after dumping to the NLCIL officials immediately after the work c ompletes. 20.0 If any loads dumped other than the locations mentioned in the out pass, the act will be seriously viewed and penal actions shall be taken including termination of the contract a s per the terms and conditions of the contract. 21.0 Rate Revision for items towards change in cost of Diesel is not applicable during the period of contra ct. 22.0 For the ash is to be transported to Mine-II Dumping yard, permission from Mines Manger shall be ob tained for plying the vehicles inside mines. Also entry permit shall be obtained from Mines manager for the crew. In the dumping yard, the contractor should make necessary arrangements for dozing th e dumping heaps by engaging suitable machineries if required. The dumping area should be maintai ned in leveled conditions. If the dumping area is not maintained in leveled conditions, penalty will be imposed as decided by the NLCIL officials. 23.0 The contractor should study the site and working conditions etc, before tendering.

24.0 As per the Directorate General of Mines safety (DGMS) circular the following safety devi ces are to be provided in Tippers deployed in the Mine. 24.1 Cabin Guard Extension / Canopy fully covering operator's cabin 24.2 Seat Belt and Seat Belt reminder 24.3 Exhaust/ Retard Brake 24.4 Propeller shaft guard 24.5 Tail gate protection 24.6 Limiting speed device 24.7 Dump Body lifted position locking arrangement 24.8 Dump Body raised position indicator with Warning 24.9 Dumb body stabilizers 24.10 Proximity warning device 24.11 Auto dipping System 24.12 load Indicator 24.13 Apart from the above, the operators should have valid VTC training. Part-II 1.0 SUPERVISOR CHARGES – PENALTY CLAUSE Not Applicable 2.0 Tools & tackles, lifting machines & Safety appliances that are used for the work or by the workmen should posses ISI mark and valid test certificate from the competent authority. 3.0 The Contractor should observe all safety rules and regulations in force and ensure that all necessar y safety precautions are followed up strictly for the safety of workers engaged in the work. 4.0 The Contractor should engage adequate man power having appropriate skills with the approval of t he NLCIL officials to carryout and complete the works. Any extra time / over time engagement of the man power shall be the contractor’s responsibility. 5.0 RATE OF WAGES The present rates of wages payable to various categories of contract workers and Supervisor are as below: TABLE Wages to be paid Total wages Category Dearness allowance-(D Rate of wages A) w.e.f 01.04.2026 (Rs. per day) (Rs. per day) (Rs. per day) USK 350.00 206 556 SSK / Supe 410.00 240 650 rvisor SK 494.00 287 781 HSK 579.00 339 918 6.0 RATE OF WAGES / DA PAYABLE TO THE WORKMEN The contractor has to pay the rates of wages / DA as per Table above as announced by NLCIL and an y revision of rates of wages / DA from time to time. However, in case of any revision of rates of wage s / DA notified during contract period, the contractor shall pay the same along with P.F. & ESI compo nent for the various categories of labour component. 7.0 RATE REVISION

(NOT APPLICABLE). 8.0 CONTRACT WORKMEN DEATH RELIEF FUND (CWDF) 8.1 An amount equivalent to 0.2% (zero point two percent) of gross value of every bill payable (b efore statutory, non statutory deductions) shall be deducted towards “Contract Workmen Deat h Relief Fund” (CWDF) from the contractors for the works carried out by the contractor. No pro vision has been made in the estimate towards the above deduction. 8.2 Based on the modified DRF scheme, monthly contributions to the death relief fund of Contract Workmen / Supervisors shall be deducted by the Contractor Employers concerned @ Rs.25/- fr om every contract workman / Supervisors engaged by Contractor Employer for the works in NL CIL from their salary /wages payable. In order to facilitate this, necessary deduction will be ma de from the bills of the Contractor employers based on Form - D (Attendance Register) & Form -B (Wage Register) Equal monthly contribution to the fund @ Rs.25/- per contract workman / S upervisors will be made by the Principal Employer NLCIL i.e. the Concerned Unit Head / Unit Ac counts Centre. 9.0 CONTRACT WORKMAN AGE The contractor shall not engage workmen beyond 60 years and the Contractor shall also produce the required age proof for the workmen engaged by him, while applying for entry permit for first time. 10.0 ESI & EPF The Contractor Employers shall be required to undertake the responsibility of re mitting the contribution/ subscription etc., of the contract workman engaged by them towards EPF (EPF & EDLI), ESI etc., (as applicable) and NLCIL as the princip al employer, will ensure compliance under the relevant applicable statutes by ve rifying the remittance made by the Contractor Employers before releasing part / final bills. 11.0 BONUS The contractor shall ensure payment of minimum bonus of 8.33% of the annual wages to the contrac t workmen engaged by them for more than 30 days subject to the wages ceiling as provided under P ayment of Bonus Act, 1965 and failure in this regard will be treated as violation of the terms of the c ontract. 12.0 SAFETY Personal protective equipments (PPE) ie like Helmet, Safety shoe, Goggles etc by to be provided by t he contractor and it is in the scope of the contractor. 13.0 PRICE REDUCTION CLAUSE Not Applicable 14.0 GUARANTEE FOR WARRANTY Not Applicable 15.0 CONTRACT PERFORMANCE GUARANTEE Not Applicable 16.0 PERIOD OF CONTRACT 11 months from service start date as per GeM contract. Note: Lead days of 3 days are provided to the Service Provider for necessary mobilization for offering servi ce. Thus the service start date will commence from minimum 3 days after contract generation date. 17.0 PAYMENT TERMS 17.1 The contractor has to submit the invoices through NeAT portal for the works carried out. After scrutiny, if it is acceptable, payment will be released to the contractor within 30 days of accept ance. 17.2 Payment will be restricted to the actual work done only based on the actual measurements a

nd as per the quoted rate in the tender schedule. 17.3 The final bill will be paid only after the finalisation of contract. 18.0 GST (Goods and Service Tax) Contractor has to furnish the GST Registration number with relevant docume ntary evidence. Contractor has to comply with the GST Act/ Rules. 19.0 NLCIL reserves the right to short close / extend the contract due to special circumstances. ***** . 3.
